The challenge in this Crl.R.P. is to the order dated 06.11.2023 in Crl.M.P. No.1120 of 2023 in C.C.
No.21 of 2023 of the Enquiry Commissioner and Special Judge, Thiruvananthapuram.
2. The petitioner, who is accused No.3, faces charges under Sections 13(1)(c) and (d) r/w Section 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 and Sections 120B and 420 of IPC.

3. The prosecution case:
Accused No.1 was the Vice President of the Pandalam Block Panchayath.
Accused No.2 was the Secretary of the Block Panchayath.

The petitioner was the Convener of the Beneficiary Committee for carrying out the work of Thonnalloor Ela Kilikolloor Punja renovation in Kadakkadu Division of the Block Panchayat under the SGRY Special Component Scheme.

The petitioner and the other accused conspired together and lifted the rice allotted for work and instead of distributing the same to the beneficiaries, the accused stored the same in the building owned by witness No.5,
sold in the black market and misappropriated the amount so obtained.
No work was carried out as per the scheme and thereby they caused loss to the Government and obtained unlawful gain.

4. The petitioner appeared before the Court Enquiry Commissioner and Special Court,
Thiruvananthapuram.

sentences.text: He filed Crl.M.P.No.1120/2023 under Section 239 Cr.P.C. and prayed for discharge.
The Trial Court dismissed the application as per the impugned order.

5. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the Revision Petitioner and the learned Senior Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondents.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner made the following submissions:
(i) The petitioner has no involvement in the alleged conspiracy.
(ii) It was accused No.1 who lifted rice from the FCI godown, Mavelikkara.
(iii) There is no prima facie material to establish that the petitioner participated in the alleged conspiracy.

2 7.
The learned Senior Public Prosecutor submitted that the prosecution material prima facie revealed the offences alleged.
The learned Public Prosecutor relied on the statements of the witnesses to substantiate that prima facie there is sufficient materials to attract the ingredients of the offences alleged.

8. The obligation to discharge the accused under Section 239 Cr.P.C. arises when the Magistrate/Special Judge considers the charge against the accused to be groundless that is, there is no legal evidence or when the facts are such that no offence is made out at all and no detailed evaluation of the materials or meticulous consideration of the possible defences need be undertaken at this stage nor any exercise of weighing materials in golden scales is to be undertaken.

{Vide:
Onkar Nath Mishra and others v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [(2008) 2 SCC 561], State of Maharashtra v. Som Nath Thapa [(1996) 4 SCC 659], State of M.P. v. Mohanlal Soni [(2000) 6 SCC 338], Sheoraj Singh Ahlawat and others v. State of Uttar Pradesh and another [(2013) 11 SCC 476],
State by Karnataka Lokayukta, Police Station, Bengaluru v. M.R.Hiremath (2019) 7 SCC 515) and State through Deputy Superintendent of Police v. R. Soundirarasu and Ors. (AIR 2022 SC 4218)}
9.

sentences.text: Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly unreasonable or there is non-consideration of any relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the Revisional Court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible.
The Revisional Court is not meant to act as an appellate court.
The whole purpose of the revisional jurisdiction is to preserve the power in the court to do justice in accordance with the principles of criminal jurisprudence.
The revisional power of the court under Sections 397 to 401 Cr.P.C is not to be equated with that of an appeal.

Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction.

{Vide: Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan v. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke [(2015) 3 SCC 123], Munna Devi v. State of Rajasthan & Anr [(2001) 9 SCC 631)] and Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd. v. Central Bureau of Investigation [(2018) 16 SCC 299)]}
10. In Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd. v. Central Bureau of Investigation [(2018) 16 SCC 299)], the Apex Court held that interference in the order framing charges or refusing to discharge is called for in the rarest of rare cases only to correct a patent error of jurisdiction.

sentences.text: 11. I shall consider the rival submissions in the light of the principles discussed above.
During 2000-2005, the Panthalam Block Panchayath had undertaken five projects under 'Sampoorna Grameena Rozgar Yojana, Special Component Scheme' in Kadakkadu Division.

Those projects were,
i. Drinking Water Project for Kuttipalavila SC Colony.
ii. Thalakkattu Chira Renovation.
iii. Cherumudi Ela Deepening.
iv. Kallarthodu, Adhikananad, Ulamayil Kadvu Renovation v. Renovation of Thonnalloor Ela-Kilikolloor Puncha.

3 12.
The subject matter of this Criminal Revision Petition relates to the allegation of misappropriation of funds in respect of Drinking Water Project in Kuttipalavila SC Colony.
The project was undertaken during 2002-2003.
A Beneficiary Committee was formed, the convener of which was the petitioner.
As per the Scheme, the Government provided 32,280 Kg. of rice worth Rs.2,00,136/- as labor component.
The rice was taken from the FCI Godown, Avaneeswaram in Kollam District.

13. The case of the prosecution is that the Block Panchayat did not execute the work but collected the rice from the FCI godown and handed over it to accused No.1, who along with the petitioner stored it in the building belonging to witness No.5 violating the Rules of SGRY Scheme.

It is the case of the prosecution that the petitioner pursuant to a conspiracy with the other accused sold the rice in black market and converted the money so obtained for their own use by cheating the Government.

The prosecution alleges that due to the acts of the petitioner and the other accused, the Government suffered a loss of Rs.2,00,136/- which the petitioner and the other accused misappropriated.
14.
Admittedly, the petitioner was the Convener of the Beneficiary Committee which had agreed to execute the work.
The prosecution relied on an acknowledgment receipt to establish that the petitioner received 23,480Kgs of food grain (rice) allotted as labour component for the work on 11.03.2003.
The statements of CWs 8 and 9 show that the work was not carried out.
The prosecution also placed material to show that the petitioner had endorsed in the Food Grain Issue Register indicating that he received the rice.
The case of the prosecution is that accused No.1 and the petitioner sold the rice in black market.

15. On analysis of the above-mentioned material, I am of the view that there are factual ingredients constituting the offences alleged and there is nothing to show that the charges levelled against the petitioner are groundless.

Therefore, the Criminal Revision Petition lacks merit and it stands dismissed.
Sd/-
